questions.stem: What is the first stage of protein synthesis called?
questions.explanation: Transcription is the first stage, where the DNA code in a gene is copied to produce a messenger RNA (mRNA) molecule in the nucleus. The mRNA then carries this code to the ribosomes for translation.
Translation occurs on ribosomes, which can be free in the cytoplasm or attached to rough endoplasmic reticulum. The ribosome reads the mRNA code and assembles amino acids into a polypeptide chain.

questions.stem: How many bases code for one amino acid?
questions.explanation: Three bases (a triplet or codon) code for one amino acid. Since there are 4 different bases, there are 64 possible triplet combinations, which is more than enough to code for the 20 different amino acids.

questions.stem: What is the role of mRNA in protein synthesis?

options.text: To carry amino acids to the ribosome
To carry the genetic code from DNA in the nucleus to the ribosome
To form the structure of the ribosome

questions.explanation: Messenger RNA (mRNA) carries a copy of the genetic code from DNA in the nucleus to the ribosomes in the cytoplasm. DNA cannot leave the nucleus, so mRNA acts as an intermediate messenger.

questions.stem: Which base replaces thymine in RNA?
questions.explanation: In RNA, the base uracil (U) replaces thymine (T). So RNA has the bases adenine, uracil, cytosine, and guanine. During transcription, where DNA has thymine, the mRNA will have adenine (and vice versa for the complement).

questions.stem: What determines the structure and function of a protein?

options.text: The sequence of amino acids, determined by the DNA base sequence
The size of the cell nucleus
The number of ribosomes in the cell

questions.explanation: The sequence of amino acids in a protein is determined by the sequence of bases in the gene (DNA). This amino acid sequence determines how the protein folds into its specific 3D shape, which determines its function.

questions.stem: Why can DNA not leave the nucleus?

options.text: Because it dissolves in the cytoplasm
Because it is attached to the cell membrane
Because it is too large and must be kept protected; mRNA carries the code instead
Because it is too small to pass through the nuclear pores

questions.explanation: DNA molecules are very large and must remain in the nucleus where they are protected. Instead, the genetic code is copied onto smaller mRNA molecules during transcription, which can pass through nuclear pores to reach the ribosomes.
